STEP 1 - Scene: A light breakfast/snack: a latte-style coffee in a white mug and a single toasted English muffin (or crumpet-like bun) on a small plate, on a tray.

STEP 2 - Vessel: Small white paper/pulp plate, roughly 15-16 cm diameter. Area ≈ 3.14 x (7.5)^2 ≈ 177 cm^2. The mug is separate from the plate.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) toasted English muffin, (b) milky coffee/latte in the mug. The mug is not part of the plated food by area, so I count the coffee separately as a drink.

STEP 4 - Area: The muffin covers roughly 25% of the plate area (~44 cm^2), which is the only food on the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Muffin is a flattened disc, about 7 cm diameter and roughly 2.5 cm thick: ~44 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 110 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like item at ~0.5 g/ml effective (muffin is airy with holes): 110 x 0.5 ≈ 55 g. Latte: mug holds about 300 ml, roughly 250 ml liquid; milk-based latte density ~1.0 g/ml, so ≈ 250 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: English muffin, toasted ≈ 230 kcal/100 g → 55 g ≈ 127 kcal. Latte with whole milk ≈ 50 kcal/100 g → 250 g ≈ 125 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One toasted muffin (~55 g) and a medium latte (~250 g, ~125 kcal) is plausible for a small breakfast. The muffin estimate is reasonable for a half-to-whole muffin of this size.
